title: PASSIVE VOICE PRACTICE & TIPS
description: Learn to use passive voice correctly in different tenses.

questions.question: Convert to passive voice: 'The chef cooks the meal.'
options: The meal is cooked by the chef.
The meal was cooked by the chef.
The meal has been cooked by the chef.
The meal will be cooked by the chef.
questions.explanation: Present simple passive: am/is/are + past participle. 'The meal is cooked by the chef.'

questions.question: Choose the correct passive form: 'The house _____ last year.'
questions.explanation: Past simple passive: was/were + past participle. 'Last year' indicates past time.

questions.question: Complete the passive: 'The project _____ by the team next month.'
questions.explanation: Future simple passive: will be + past participle. 'Next month' indicates future time.

questions.question: Convert to passive: 'They are building a new bridge.'
options: A new bridge is being built.
A new bridge was being built.
A new bridge has been built.
A new bridge will be built.
questions.explanation: Present continuous passive: am/is/are being + past participle.

questions.question: Choose the correct form: 'The letter _____ yesterday.'
questions.explanation: Past simple passive: was/were + past participle. 'Yesterday' indicates past time.

questions.question: Complete: 'The work _____ by tomorrow.'
questions.explanation: Future simple passive: will be + past participle. 'By tomorrow' indicates future completion.

questions.question: Convert to passive: 'Someone has stolen my car.'
questions.explanation: Present perfect passive: has/have been + past participle.

questions.question: Choose the correct form: 'The book _____ in many languages.'
questions.explanation: Present perfect passive for actions completed in the past with present relevance.

questions.question: Complete: 'The meeting _____ at 3 PM.'
questions.explanation: Future simple passive: will be + past participle for scheduled future events.

title: Academic Writing: Passive Voice
description: Advanced passive voice practice for academic writing contexts.

questions.question: Convert to academic passive: 'Researchers conducted the study.'
options: The study was conducted by researchers.
The study is conducted by researchers.
The study has been conducted by researchers.
The study will be conducted by researchers.
questions.explanation: Academic writing often uses passive voice to focus on the research rather than the researchers.

questions.question: Choose the correct academic form: 'The results _____ in the next section.'
questions.explanation: Future passive is common in academic writing to indicate what will be covered next.

title: Complex Passive Voice: Advanced Practice
description: Master complex passive voice constructions including modal passives and causative passives.

questions.question: Convert to passive: 'You must complete this form.'
questions.explanation: Modal passive: modal + be + past participle. 'Must be completed' is the correct form.

questions.question: Choose the correct form: 'The work _____ by Friday.'
questions.explanation: Modal passive: should + be + past participle. 'Should be finished' is correct.

questions.question: Complete: 'The report _____ by the committee yesterday.'
questions.explanation: Past continuous passive: was/were being + past participle for actions in progress in the past.

questions.question: Convert to passive: 'Someone might have stolen the money.'
options: The money might have been stolen.
questions.explanation: Modal perfect passive: modal + have been + past participle. 'Might have been stolen' is correct.

questions.question: Choose the correct form: 'The building _____ for years.'
questions.explanation: Present perfect continuous passive: has/have been being + past participle for ongoing actions.

questions.question: Complete: 'The documents _____ by the lawyer right now.'
questions.explanation: Present continuous passive: am/is/are being + past participle for actions in progress now.

questions.question: Convert to passive: 'They had already finished the project.'
options: The project had already been finished.
The project has already been finished.
questions.explanation: Past perfect passive: had been + past participle for actions completed before another past action.

questions.question: Choose the correct form: 'The problem _____ by the engineers next week.'
questions.explanation: Future simple passive: will be + past participle for future actions.

questions.question: Complete: 'The house _____ when we arrived.'
questions.explanation: Past continuous passive: was/were being + past participle for actions in progress in the past.

questions.question: Convert to passive: 'People speak English all over the world.'
options: English is spoken all over the world.
English was spoken all over the world.
English has been spoken all over the world.
English will be spoken all over the world.
questions.explanation: Present simple passive: am/is/are + past participle for general statements.

questions.question: Choose the correct form: 'The meeting _____ by the manager tomorrow.'
questions.explanation: Future simple passive: will be + past participle for scheduled future events.

questions.question: Complete: 'The car _____ by the mechanic right now.'
questions.explanation: Present continuous passive: am/is/are being + past participle for actions in progress now.

questions.question: Convert to passive: 'They will have completed the work by then.'
options: The work will have been completed by then.
The work will be completed by then.
The work has been completed by then.
The work was completed by then.
questions.explanation: Future perfect passive: will have been + past participle for actions completed before a future time.

questions.question: Choose the correct form: 'The book _____ by millions of readers.'
questions.explanation: Present perfect passive: has/have been + past participle for actions with present relevance.

questions.question: Complete: 'The decision _____ by the board yesterday.'
questions.explanation: Past simple passive: was/were + past participle for completed actions in the past.
